title: Resolving the Magnetic Ground State and Field-Induced Transitions in Magnetic Dirac Semimetal Candidate EuMnSb$_2$
authors: Yiu-Fung Chiu, Jian-Rui Soh, Sanjay Sharma, J. Alberto Rodríguez-Velamazán, John Singleton, Eugen Weschke, Oleksandr Prokhnenko, Oksana Zaharko, Dharmalingam Prabhakaran, Stephen J. Blundell, Paul A. Goddard, Andrew T. Boothroyd
abstract: The magnetic structure of a magnetic topological semimetal EuMnSb$_2$ is investigated in fields up to 30 T using polarized and unpolarized neutron diffraction, pulsed-field x-ray magnetic circular dichroism and pulsed-field magnetometry. We determine the zero-field magnetic structures of the Eu and Mn sublattices, and find that magnetic transitions induced by applied fields below 2 T correspond to changes in the magnetic order of the Eu spins alone without detectable perturbation to the order of the Mn spins. An additional magnetic transition is observed at fields close to the saturation field for the Eu spins. We present a mean-field model which describes key features of the magnetic behavior and allows us to estimate the dominant Eu--Eu and Eu--Mn exchange interactions responsible for the coupling between magnetism and electronic topology.
summary: This work investigates the intricate magnetic ordering and field response of $	ext{EuMnSb}_2$, a candidate Dirac semimetal. By combining advanced neutron scattering, XMCD, and magnetometry, the authors determine that Eu spins undergo transitions independently of the Mn sublattice at low fields. They model these interactions using an effective Hamiltonian to quantify the coupling between magnetism and electronic topology.
main_problem: The study aims to resolve the magnetic ground state and understand field-induced transitions within the magnetic Dirac semimetal candidate $	ext{EuMnSb}_2$.
main_result: Magnetic transitions observed below 2 T are attributed solely to changes in Eu spin order, while Mn spins remain largely unaffected. A mean-field model was developed to estimate key Eu--Eu and Eu--Mn exchange interactions.
method: The research combines multiple experimental techniques including polarized/unpolarized neutron diffraction, pulsed-field XMCD, magnetometry, and AC transport measurements, supplemented by developing a mean-field theoretical model.
model_or_system: The system is the magnetic topological semimetal $	ext{EuMnSb}_2$, featuring coupled Eu and Mn magnetic sublattices. The modeling involves an effective spin Hamiltonian incorporating nearest-neighbor AFM and FM exchange interactions, along with external fields.
key_observables: Magnetic structure (via neutron diffraction), magnetization $M(H)$, susceptibility $\chi(T)$, and specific field-induced transitions ($	ext{Hc1}, 	ext{Hc2}$).
important_parameters: Applied magnetic fields up to 30 T; temperatures down to 1.8 K.
main_assumptions: The Mn sublattice is treated as an effectively rigid background structure (C-type AFM). The mean-field model provides a first approximation of the complex spin interactions.
figures_summary: Figures compare magnetic structures determined by different methods and highlight field dependence, showing transitions in magnetization curves along $a$ and $c$ axes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence from multiple measurements (neutron diffraction, XMCD, magnetometry) to establish the magnetic structure. It then develops a mean-field model based on these findings to quantify the dominant exchange interactions coupling magnetism and electronic topology.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the study of coupled spin systems under external fields and the development of effective Hamiltonians for complex magnetic order parameters are relevant to understanding quantum many-body dynamics in strongly correlated materials.

Figure 2(a) shows the zero-field c-axis resistivity of our Sn-flux-grown crystal. The resistivity increases strongly with decreasing temperature, confirming that the sample belongs to the semiconducting rather than metallic class of EuMnSb2 crystals [9, 18]. A shoulder in the tempera- ture dependence is observed near TEu1 ≃21 K, consistent with the coupling between charge transport and the suc- cessive magnetic transitions of the Eu sublattice. This overall behaviour agrees with previous transport mea- surements on Sn-flux-grown EuMnSb2 [9, 18].
